research.summary: Archive acquisition/extraction is a fail-closed network-independent core. ORACC publishes no authenticated checksum, so previously unseen bytes require two independent fetch streams with identical byte length and SHA-256. Project roots are derived from internal metadata.json location plus declared pathname/project, including three-level projects; live HTTP/TLS ownership remains outside PH3.

design.boundary: Bounded stream-to-temp acquisition, two-fetch corroboration, ZIP structural/resource preflight, portable path validation, structure-derived ORACC project roots, manual staged extraction, atomic destination publication, and cleanup only. No live HTTP client, discovery policy, lock mutation, source diff, rebuild, or release publication.
design.security_contract: Reject unsafe/non-portable paths, duplicate/casefold/prefix aliases, symlinks and special files, encryption, unsupported compression, classic-ZIP structural inconsistencies, member/aggregate/ratio resource exhaustion, and extraction length disagreement before publishing any destination tree. ZIP64 requires an explicit research/design update rather than silent widening.

functional_green.generated_reference_result: Real checked-in corpus build and generated-reference consistency passed.

behavior.acquisition: Download chunks are byte-capped while written once and hashed; unseen bytes are accepted only after two independently supplied streams agree in length and SHA-256; mismatch or second-fetch failure cleans temporary copies.
behavior.preflight: Classic ZIP EOCD facts are bounded-read, the central directory is sequentially scanned and member-capped before ZipFile materialization, scanned count is cross-checked against EOCD and materialized entries, and ZIP64/multidisk inputs fail closed pending explicit research.
behavior.paths: Member/project components require NFC relative POSIX paths and reject traversal, backslashes, Windows forbidden characters, trailing dot/space, reserved device names, casefold aliases at full-path and ancestor-prefix levels, and file/directory prefix collisions.
behavior.extraction: All members are manually copied only after complete preflight into an isolated sibling staging tree with actual decompressed byte accounting; destination publication is one final rename and failed staging trees are removed.

independent_review.result: Fresh logically-independent security re-review found no remaining blocker inside PH3's declared remote-archive threat boundary after the portable-path and forged-EOCD hardening. Durable evidence addition requires a new exact-head validation and final re-review before this core can be considered blocked-ready.

completion_blocker.reason: PH3's network-independent security core is implemented and tested, but completion requires integration with PH2's discovery/download transport path; PH2 itself remains completion-blocked by PH1 normal-TLS upstream acquisition. No TLS verification may be weakened to satisfy this dependency.

resume_gate: After PH2/PH1 authenticated transport is available, connect the real downloaded archive stream to acquire_unseen/preflight/extract without relaxing any fail-closed rule, exercise representative active RIAO/RINAP inputs plus a three-level project, record integration evidence, then run exact-head CI and a fresh independent security review before marking P-002.PH3 done.
